key_insight: MedGraph uses graph memory to track changing patient information, distinguish whose facts are whose, and keep recorded safety facts available across medical conversations.
clinical_relevance: More reliable longitudinal memory could help medical assistants avoid answers based on outdated states, another person’s history, or missing safety information.
method: Extract dated, person-attributed facts from each dialogue session.
Link medication, diagnosis, and measurement records into chains that preserve earlier states.
Retrieve patient-specific chains for the requested time, add original dialogue text, and include all recorded safety facts.
evidence_signal: On MedMemoryBench, MedGraph achieved the highest overall accuracy against five baselines with GPT and Qwen backbones, improving on the strongest baseline by 10.5 and 10.4 points, respectively.
watch_item: Benchmark gains do not establish clinical safety; performance still depends on correctly extracting, dating, and attributing patient facts.
paper_title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
